# Model card: TrustGate signup-abuse model

**Task.** Given a signup (email, device fingerprint, device type, how often this device signed up before), estimate the
probability that it belongs to free-trial abuse. The API turns that into a 0-100 score on the same scale as the rule engine.
The final score is the higher of the two. If the model files are missing the rules decide alone.

**Training data. Synthetic, generated by us.** `training/generate_synthetic.py` simulates 150,000 signups over 30 days
(8% abusive). It encodes our assumptions: abusers run campaigns of 2-12 signups, use auto-generated email names and
disposable domains more often, and a quarter of them rotate their device fingerprint. Honest users sometimes share a device
or use a disposable address. In the last 20% of the timeline abusers adapt (fewer disposable domains, more name-like emails).
No real users and no third-party fraud dataset were used.

**Features.** email on the disposable list (CC0 list), email-domain frequency, email-name length, digit ratio of the email name,
device type, and four per-device velocity counters (earlier signups, seconds since the last one, same hour, same day).
Training and the API share the same email-feature code (`backend/app/features.py`), and a test checks that the velocity
features match between training and serving.

**Method.** LightGBM, time-ordered split (oldest 60% train, next 20% early stopping and calibration, newest 20% test),
isotonic calibration, thresholds picked on the validation slice (flag at about 2% of honest signups, block at 90% precision).
Per-decision reasons come from LightGBM's own feature contributions.

**Results on the synthetic test slice (newest 20%).**

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| ROC-AUC | 0.957 |
| PR-AUC | 0.858 |
| Abuse caught at 1% false alarms | 73.6% |
| At the flag threshold: precision / recall | 76.2% / 78.7% |
| At the block threshold: precision / recall | 88.2% / 72.9% |
| Disposable-email list alone: precision / recall | 62.0% / 31.3% |

(Exact values are in `backend/app/model/model_meta.json` after you run `python training/train.py`.)

**What these numbers mean.** They show the pipeline works end to end and that a model combining several weak signals beats the
list alone **on data that follows our assumptions**. They are not an estimate of accuracy on real customers. Real attackers behave
differently, and real data would change every figure.

**Known limits.** Synthetic data. No IP, geo or payment-method features in the model (the rule engine has a small datacenter-IP
heuristic). Needs retraining as abuse patterns drift. Name-like emails from a clean device will pass. Honest users on shared
devices or with privacy-focused emails can be flagged, which is why "flag" means a one-time code, not a ban.

**How to improve it for real use.** Train on labelled outcomes from a real product (chargebacks, confirmed trial abuse, manual
reviews), add payment-side signals, and monitor drift.
